passage: I am Simran and I sit next to Maria. Today our teacher said, "Well done, Maria, you tried so hard on that sum," and stuck a gold star on her page. Maria sat up straight and her cheeks went pink. She looked at the star for a long time. At break she asked for the harder page instead of the easy one. I do not know what she felt exactly, but she looked tall and happy to me.

qa.q: What did the teacher stick on Maria's page?
qa.a: The teacher stuck a gold star on her page.

qa.q: What does Maria's choice of the harder page suggest about how the praise affected her?
qa.a: It suggests she felt proud and keen to keep trying, because she was praised for effort. She did not seem afraid of a mistake.

qa.q: Why is "you tried so hard" a better kind of praise than "you are the best"?
qa.a: It tells her that effort is what counts, so a mistake does not threaten her. Praise only for being best can make a child fear errors. 😊

qa.q: How does Simran's own account limit what we can know about Maria?
qa.a: Simran only saw Maria's straight back, pink cheeks and choice, and says Simran does not know exactly what Maria felt. It is an outside guess.

grounding: The teacher says well done, you tried so hard, and gives me a star; I feel tall and happy and want to keep trying.

passage:
Monday. Sumit, five, tried hard to cut along the line. His paper was crooked. Vasudha Miss said, "Well done, you tried so hard!" and gave him a star.

Wednesday. Sumit tried again, slower. He felt tall and happy.

Friday. His cut was almost straight. He showed it to Miss before anyone else. "I kept trying!" Miss smiled. "You did."

qa.q: What did Vasudha Miss give Sumit on Monday?
qa.a: Vasudha Miss gave him a star.

qa.q: What was Sumit feeling on Wednesday?
qa.a: Sumit felt proud and happy, tall inside because of the praise.

qa.q: Why did the teacher's praise help Sumit improve?
qa.a: She praised his effort, not just the result, which made him keep trying.

qa.q: How might Vasudha Miss feel on Friday?
qa.a: She likely feels pleased and proud to see Sumit's progress.

grounding: Shows a young child who beams at praise for effort and keeps trying.

passage:
The rain was so loud on the tin roof that Avni Ma'am had to raise her voice. Bhupen, five, kept trying to write his name. The B kept tipping over.

Avni Ma'am knelt beside him. "You've written it four times. Well done, you kept trying!" She drew a star on his hand.

Bhupen felt tall and happy. He wrote it once more, slowly. The B stood up straight.

qa.q: What did Avni Ma'am draw on Bhupen's hand?
qa.a: Avni Ma'am drew a star on his hand.

qa.q: What was Bhupen feeling when he got the star?
Why was Avni Ma'am's praise helpful?
qa.a: She praised his effort in trying again, which made him keep trying instead of fearing mistakes.

qa.q: How might Avni Ma'am feel when the B stands up straight?
qa.a: She likely feels glad that her praise encouraged him.

grounding: Shows a young child who feels proud after praise for effort and keeps trying.
